title: Lusin–Souslin: Borel image and Borel left inverse of a map that is continuous and injective on a Borel set (supplied step 5)
statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let H : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, and let B ⊆ ℝⁿ be Borel such that H is continuous on B (ContinuousOn H B) and injective on B (InjOn H B). Then H(B) is Borel, and there is a Borel measurable map h : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ with h(H(u)) = u for every u ∈ B.
lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (H : Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : Set (Euclid n)), ContinuousOn H B → MeasurableSet B → InjOn H B → MeasurableSet (H '' B) ∧ ∃ h : Euclid P → Euclid n, Measurable h ∧ ∀ u ∈ B, h (H u) = u
